title: Design a Chat/Messaging System (like WhatsApp): WebSocket for real-time, message storage, delivery status (sent/delivered/read), group chat, end-to-end encryption, offline message queuing.
keyPoints: WebSocket connections provide bidirectional, real-time message delivery; a presence registry maps users to their server.
Persist every message before attempting delivery so a server crash never loses it (persist-first rule).
Delivery status is a state machine: sent (persisted) -> delivered (device ack) -> read (user opens chat).
Offline queuing stores messages for disconnected users and flushes them in order on reconnect.
Group chat fans a message to all members, either by per-member inbox copies or a shared reference.
End-to-end encryption means the client encrypts with the recipient's public key; the server stores only ciphertext.
Messages carry monotonic sequence numbers per conversation for gap detection and duplicate rejection.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a live WebSocket per user for instant delivery, persist every message, track sent-delivered-read ticks, and queue messages for offline users.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **WebSocket** : a persistent bidirectional connection for real-time message push without polling.
- **Presence registry** : maps each connected user to the server holding their socket (usually Redis).
- **Delivery status** : a state machine tracking sent, delivered, and read states via acknowledgements.
- **Offline queuing** : stores messages for disconnected users and delivers them in order on reconnect.
- **End-to-end encryption (E2EE)** : the client encrypts the message so only the recipient's device can decrypt it; the server sees only ciphertext.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India adds a secure in-app chat so Rajesh can talk to his relationship manager Priya about a loan. When both are online, messages appear instantly. When Priya is away, the bank holds Rajesh's messages and delivers them when she returns. Rajesh sees ticks: sent, delivered, read. Because it is banking, only they can read the contents.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A chat system delivers messages in real time using WebSockets, persists every message before delivery, tracks delivery status through sent-delivered-read, and queues messages for offline users. The persist-first rule is non-negotiable: a crash must never lose a message.

Delivery status is a small state machine driven by acknowledgements. Offline queuing holds messages for disconnected users and flushes in order on reconnect. End-to-end encryption means the server only stores ciphertext.

At National Bank of India, this powered secure chat between customers and relationship managers, where offline queuing and delivery ticks were essential for trust.

Remember one sentence: persist every message before delivery, use WebSockets for real-time push, track sent-delivered-read status, and queue for offline users with end-to-end encryption for banking privacy.
